Full-Time · Remote (Lahore) · $1,500-$2,200 USD/month Hours: U.S. business hours (Pacific/Central), Monday-Friday

About RevStone

RevStone is a U.S.-based managed staffing company. We place trained, World-Wide-based Operators into growing American businesses. We are not a VA marketplace. We are your employer on this side - we handle payroll, benefits, and support, and we back you with SOPs, training, and a real team lead who has your back.

About the Client
You'll be placed full-time with a fast-growing U.S. digital marketing agency that builds and manages websites for a portfolio of small and mid-sized business clients across multiple industries. They need one person who owns SEO across all of those client sites - not a task-taker, but the agency's in-house SEO expert.

The Role
This is a "Swiss Army knife" SEO role. You won't be working on one website. You'll be working across a portfolio of client sites built on different platforms - WordPress, Webflow, Shopify, and others - and you need to be comfortable jumping between them without hand-holding.
One day you're fixing crawl errors on a Webflow site. The next you're building out a local SEO plan for a service business, writing content briefs for an e-commerce client, and presenting a monthly report to the agency's account manager. If that sounds like fun instead of chaos, keep reading.

What You'll Own

• Technical SEO across all client sites: audits, Core Web Vitals, crawl and indexing issues, redirects, site architecture, schema markup

• Platform-specific implementation on WordPress (Yoast/RankMath, page builders) and Webflow (CMS collections, custom code embeds, SEO settings), plus Shopify and other builders as needed

• Keyword research and search intent mapping for clients in very different industries

• On-page SEO: titles, metas, headers, internal linking, content optimization

• Local SEO for service-based clients: Google Business Profile, citations, service-area and location pages

• Content strategy: briefs and content calendars that writers can execute

• Link building and digital PR outreach

• New website launches: SEO migration checklists so clients don't lose rankings when a site is rebuilt

• Reporting: Google Search Console, GA4, Ahrefs/Semrush - rankings, traffic, conversions, clearly explained

• Being the SEO voice inside the agency: telling account managers what each client needs next and why

You're a Fit If You Have

• 4+ years of hands-on SEO experience, ideally in an agency environment managing multiple client accounts at once

• Proven results you can show with screenshots (GSC, Ahrefs, Semrush, or similar)

• Real, hands-on experience with both WordPress and Webflow - you've built or optimized live sites on each

• Strong technical SEO fundamentals: you can read a crawl report, diagnose why something isn't indexing, and fix it yourself

• Working knowledge of HTML/CSS and the ability to implement schema and technical fixes without waiting on a developer

• Fluency with Google Search Console, GA4, and Ahrefs or Semrush

• Excellent written and spoken English - you'll communicate directly with the U.S. team and occasionally clients

• The ability to work U.S. hours consistently with reliable internet and backup power

• Strong organization: you can juggle 10+ client accounts and know what's due on each without being reminded

Nice to Have

• Experience with Shopify, Squarespace, Wix, or GoHighLevel websites

• E-commerce SEO experience (product pages, collection pages, faceted navigation)

• Familiarity with AI search / generative engine optimization (AI Overviews, ChatGPT search visibility)

• Experience running or supporting Google Ads / Local Service Ads

• Basic understanding of CRO and landing page optimization

What You Get

title: Machine Learning Engineer
description:
Job Summary

We are seeking a highly motivated and experienced Machine Learning Engineer to join our dynamic and growing Data Platforms & Solutions team. As a Machine Learning Engineer at Viking you will design, productionize, deploy, and operate machine learning solutions that support management decisions.

This role bridges data science, data engineering, and software engineering. You will work closely with data scientists, data engineers, analysts, product partners, and software developers to translate experimental models into scalable, reliable, governed production systems on Databricks. The position emphasizes practical MLOps, robust feature and training pipelines, reproducibility, observability, and measurable business outcomes.

Job Responsibilities:

• Design, build, deploy, and maintain production-grade machine learning solutions supporting demand forecasting, dynamic pricing, inventory optimization, and recommendation use cases.

• Partner with data scientists to convert experimental notebooks and prototypes into modular, tested, repeatable training and inference pipelines.

• Build and maintain feature engineering, model-training, batch-scoring, and real-time inference workflows using Python, Spark, SQL, Databricks, and MLflow.

• Implement MLOps practices for experiment tracking, model registration and versioning, automated testing, CI/CD, controlled promotion, rollback, and reproducibility.

• Define and monitor model and operational health measures, including model quality, drift signals, latency, failures, data quality, resource utilization, and compute cost.

• Validate model changes against reproducible datasets and established baselines, and assess downstream impact.

• Integrate model outputs with business applications and downstream platforms through reliable batch jobs, APIs, and secure data-access patterns.

• Optimize model architecture, feature processing, training, and inference for scalability, reliability, maintainability, and cost efficiency.

• Implement safeguards and fallback behavior so invalid data or failed optimization does not result in unsafe or misleading recommendations.

• Collaborate with stakeholders to translate revenue-management requirements into technical specifications, acceptance criteria, and measurable outcomes.

• Create and maintain technical documentation, model cards, runbooks, deployment plans, monitoring procedures, and retraining and rollback strategies.

• Ensure solutions comply with enterprise data governance, privacy, security, audit, and responsible AI requirements.

Job Requirements:

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Data Science, Statistics, Applied Mathematics, or a related field; or equivalent practical experience.

• 4+ years of relevant experience in machine learning engineering, applied data science, data engineering, or software engineering for production ML systems.

• Strong proficiency in Python and SQL, including experience building maintainable, testable production code.

• Hands-on experience developing, deploying, and supporting machine learning models in production environments.

• Experience with cloud platforms, with a preference for Microsoft Azure.

• Experience with Apache Spark or Databricks and large-scale data processing.

• Knowledge of supervised learning, forecasting, optimization, feature engineering, model evaluation, and experiment design.

• Experience with software engineering practices including Git, code review, automated testing, CI/CD, configuration management, and environment promotion.

• Strong problem-solving, critical-thinking, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills.

• Ability to work independently, manage changing priorities, and deliver in a fast-paced product environment.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Experience designing batch and real-time model-serving patterns and integrating model outputs into operational applications.

• Experience with model explainability techniques,

title: IDRA Research Fellow
description:
IDRA is an independent, non-profit organization, led by Celina Moreno, J.D. Our mission is to achieve equal educational opportunity for every child through strong public schools that prepare all students to access and succeed in college.
We are seeking a talented research fellow to provide cross-functional support to IDRA ’s research and evaluation team by delivering timely analytical products that support the work of IDRA and its various projects.
The research fellow will be responsible for collecting data from a variety of sources; manipulating, organizing, cleaning and cross-checking data; preparing reports; and presenting data to key stakeholders. The research fellow will be expected to participate in strategy discussions and research team meetings; contribute to advocacy, outreach or education practice work; and assist with administrative or project coordination tasks. A successful candidate will be technically proficient in research development and statistical analysis.
To be eligible, fellowship applicants must:

• Commit to a full-time fellowship starting September 2026 and ending August 2027.

• Have earned a degree in a quantitative field such as economics, social sciences, statistics, public policy, business administration or related field.

• Be able to travel to conduct multi-day site visits at higher education institutions in the continental United States and U.S. territories (approximately one to two visits per month).

• Have an interest in learning multiple facets of evaluation, including data analysis and research and on-the-ground site visits.

• Possess a strong ability to learn new concepts and tools quickly.

• Demonstrate excellent writing skills for various purposes and audiences.

• Be willing to teach and share knowledge and skills, including those gained during the fellowship, with students, families, IDRA staff and fellows, and other partners.

• Possess a commitment to building relationships with young people, families, teachers and other public education and higher education advocates.

• Be committed to expanding access to excellent pre-K-12 and to college access and completion opportunities for all students, particularly students of color, immigrant students, students from families with limited incomes and other historically-marginalized groups.

• Demonstrate strong interpersonal skills, including engaging with stakeholders from a range of backgrounds, such as partners from federal agencies, higher education, K-12, and non-profit organizations.

Required skills include:

• Graduate degree, Ph.D. preferred (or five years of experience working in a related field).

• Proven knowledge and application of research methods and assessment practices.

• Strong technical and data analytical skills.

• Strong verbal, written and interpersonal communication skills.

• Experience in data collection and statistical reporting.

• Proficiency with statistical software, such as MS Excel, R (Posit), and/or Dedoose.

• Experience with survey tools, such as Qualtrics and/or Survey Monkey.

• Experience with quantitative and qualitative research.

Preferred skills include:

• Knowledge of education data sets (Texas Education Agency, U.S. Department of Education, American Community Survey, Census Summary Files).

• Experience working with confidential information within established guidelines.

Salary is $75,000 or higher, commensurate with experience, plus contribution toward medical insurance.
Application Process
To apply, submit the following:

• Completed application form

• Cover letter

• Curriculum vita or resumé

• Writing sample

• Contact information for two professional references

Application deadline: September 18, 2026
IDRA ’s research fellowship is open to all eligible applicants regardless of race, national origin, religion, gender, age, ability or sexual orientation.

What began as a boutique design studio has evolved into one of the fastest-growing private companies in America (Inc. 5000) and among the most effective performance media agencies of the 2020s (Varos). Our founders were recognized by Forbes 30 Under 30 for advancing the intersection of technology, marketing, and advertising, cementing Darkroom's role as a defining player in the future of media innovation.

About the Role

Darkroom owns creator strategy for the brands we work with, and more of them now want a community behind it: creators, customers, and fans who post because they want to, not because a brief told them to. This role builds those communities from zero and runs them as a growth channel.

A community here is measured on what it produces outside itself: posts, content, referrals, and signups or sales. Most of our communities are tiered. A small inner circle of top creators gets money, early access, and a direct line to the brand. A larger ambassador tier gets access, perks, and first look at launches. Program tiers, like campus leaders or customer champions, run their own threads. And the open community is where everyone else joins. You decide how people get in, what each tier gets, what happens every week, and how activity turns into output.

This is a consumer role. The people in these communities are students, parents, professionals, and fans, and a community run like a support forum or a developer channel will not work here.

You report to a Director and work alongside the creator leads, the social team, paid media, and each client's product and brand teams.

This role is based in New York, working US hours, with travel for events.

What You'll Do

Build new communities

- Choose the platform for each community (usually Discord, sometimes Slack, WhatsApp, Geneva, Circle, or a subreddit) and stand it up: channel architecture, roles and permissions, bots, onboarding, tier assignment, and moderation rules.

- Set the entry rules and the offer for each tier with the creator leads and the client, such as free product for creators over a follower threshold, student access, or referral perks.

- Build a proof channel before launch, where members show what the product did for them. It is the flex wall, and the best posts get reposted by the brand.

Run it every week

- Welcome new members, assign tiers, and post open briefs in #briefs with a clear view of who claimed what and when it is due.

- Run the 1-in-20 triage: find the post that popped, work out why, and brief the rest of the roster on it the same week.

- Repost the top receipts and hand the best ones to the social and paid teams.

- Give members a real line to the brand. Route product questions, feedback, and bug reports to the client's team and bring the answers back.

- Monthly: an AMA with someone from the brand, program leaderboards, and a roster health check (who is posting, who has gone quiet, and what you do about it).

title: Operations Manager, Operative Acquisition
description:
Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. Backed by Europe’s largest-ever logistics Series A ($35M) led by deep-tech investors Plural, and a recently closed Series B ($95M), Relay is scaling faster than 99% of venture-backed startups. We're assembling the most talent-dense team the logistics industry has ever seen

Relay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction. Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people, making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone.

THE TEAM
• ~160 people, around half in engineering, product and data
• 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research
• Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle
• An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking, tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation

THE ROLE

Every parcel through our sort centres is handled by an operative. At peak, we need to hire up to 600 of them a week.

As Operations Manager, Operative Acquisition you'll own operative supply across our sortation sites: enough suitable, trained, compliant and active operatives to fill every shift. You'll build the funnel, reporting and automation that make supply repeatable rather than manual, and keep it ahead of demand as volume rises.

Volumes rise sharply into November and December. Supply, not demand, will be the constraint. This role exists to make sure it isn't.

You'll be the single owner of the operative funnel, working across acquisition (including paid channels), Live Operations, our site teams, and Product and Engineering, who build the integrations the funnel runs on. You'll write SQL, ship automation, and spend time at our sort centres seeing how new starters actually land.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Own the operative funnel end to end, from applicant attraction through qualification, training, activation and retention

- Keep applicant supply ahead of site demand, forecasting how many applicants, training places and sessions are needed and directing spend where gaps exist

- Improve qualification and compliance, owning Right to Work/KYC and working with Product and Engineering to reduce drop-off and speed up the process

- Optimise training capacity and waitlists, making sure sessions are filled and candidates stay engaged

- Get new starters onto shift quickly, supporting activation, shift fill, communications and low-fill processes

- Reduce cancellations, no-shows and inactivity, using the root causes to improve communications, processes and policies

- Own operative communications and compliance processes, including waitlist messaging, suspensions, strikes and shift-booking comms

- Build clear funnel reporting and alerts, tracking volumes, conversion, time to hire and drop-off by site to identify issues early

WHO WILL THRIVE IN THIS ROLE?

- A growth or operations background. You treat supply as a daily number and act the same day it slips

- Confident in SQL (BigQuery or similar). You build dashboards from raw data, not static trackers

- Experience running a high-volume hiring or onboarding funnel, ideally for a frontline workforce

- Comfortable with paid acquisition, Google Ads or similar, enough to read performance and brief changes when a site runs short

- Hands-on with automation, setting up triggers for invitations, comms and alerts, and quick to get confident in a new ATS or scheduling system

- A working understanding of Right to Work checks, enough to see how checks and re-checks affect the funnel and operative status. Legal owns the detail, but this can't be a blank

- Clear writing. You can write processes, requirements and comms that other teams rely on

Desirable

- Experience onboarding couriers or drivers at a carrier or delivery platform

title: Accountant

description:
ABOUT FLUIDSTACK

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.

We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

HOW WE OPERATE

- Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

- Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

- Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

- Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

- Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

HOW WE OPERATE

- Extreme ownership. Full autonomy. Own things end to end often taking on scope outside your core role without being asked to get things done.

- Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

THE INFRASTRUCTURE TEAM

Examples of key problems the team is working on

- Design the physical layer AGI is trained on. ISP/OSP cable plants carry hundreds of thousands of fiber terminations per building, rail-optimized for the densest GPU fabrics ever built, at 800G today and 1.6T next.

- One design, every site. Turn the cable plant from a bespoke months-long exercise into a stamped reference architecture deployed across 10s to 100s of GWs of capacity, validated once and built everywhere.

- Design for silicon that doesn't exist yet. Every GPU generation rewrites the density, optics, and pathway math, but the plant you spec must survive three of them.

ROLE SCOPE

- Own the end-to-end physical implementation of the data center network: fiber plant architecture, transceiver planning, and structured cabling integration for hyperscale sites.

- Collaborate with CSA, MEP, and construction teams on power, cooling, space, pathways, cabinets, and racks, and develop, read, and interpret construction drawings in Bluebeam, ACC, and Procore.

- Break down DCN logical port maps (TOR, spine, super-spine, DCI) into physical cross-connect and patching schedules, and automate port-to-fiber mapping at 100K+ ports per site.

- Define cassette types (MTP/MPO Base-8/12/16), trunk counts, and structured cabling hierarchy, and model fiber utilization and overbuild for two to three hardware generations.

- Select optics (400G/800G DR4, FR4, LR4, SR8, coherent DCI) by reach and loss budget, validate interoperability across vendors and generations, and maintain loss-budget and margin models for every link type.

- Own the ICT Basis of Design, SOPs, and Division 26/27/28/33 master specifications, and integrate with DCIM (NetBox, custom tools) to track strands, ports, and patching.

title: Hardware Field Quality Engineer Intern (Summer 2027)
description:
At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. Lyft Urban Solutions designs, builds, and operates bikeshare systems in more than 50 cities worldwide, including New York, Chicago, London, Barcelona, Mexico City, Rio de Janeiro, and Montréal. Our Longueuil facility is the birthplace of BIXI, North America's first automated bikeshare system, and today builds the bikes and stations behind some of the world's largest bikeshare networks.

We are looking for a Hardware Field Quality Engineer Intern to join our Field Quality team at our Longueuil facility. Once our bikes, e-bikes, batteries, and stations leave the factory, Field Quality owns how they hold up in the real world: millions of rides, all four seasons, in cities across the globe. You will work alongside field quality engineers to help spot emerging hardware issues, investigate their root cause, and support fixes with engineering, manufacturing, and market operations teams. You will spend time hands-on with failed parts in the lab, and just as much time in the data working out how big a problem really is.

• Support failure analysis on parts returned from the field, including requests from enterprise customers, by helping with teardown, inspection, and electrical testing and documenting findings with photos.

• Help monitor field data, such as vehicle and station alerts and repair records, and flag emerging issues to the team.

• Build and update dashboards and queries that track reliability metrics and retrofit progress.

• Assist with field retrofit campaigns by helping identify affected units and tracking progress.

• Help review repair SOPs and troubleshooting guides used by market mechanics, and suggest improvements.

• Contribute to field failure investigations in Jira, working with engineers on root cause and corrective actions.

• Professional proficiency in French and English , written and spoken (required)

• Hands-on comfort with electromechanical hardware, including disassembly, inspection, and basic electrical troubleshooting with tools like a multimeter

• Strong analytical skills and comfort working with large, imperfect datasets to reach clear conclusions

• Familiarity with structured problem-solving methods (5 Whys, fishbone diagrams, 8D, FMEA)

• Curious and detail-oriented, with clear written communication

• Previous internship or co-op in quality, reliability, test, or failure analysis is a plus

• SQL or Python, and experience with Mode, Hex, Tableau, or Power BI, is a plus

• Exposure to e-bikes, batteries, automotive, or other electromechanical products, or to reading wiring diagrams, is a plus

title: Applied Science Manager
description:
ABOUT CLIPBOARD

Our mission is to uplift as many communities as possible. We do this through our app-based marketplace that connects healthcare professionals with the workplaces that need amazing workers. This enables hundreds of thousands of people to achieve financial stability for themselves and their families while providing essential care to millions of people across the U.S.

Founded in 2016, we are a remote-first team of over 1,000 people building a top Y-Combinator company https://www.ycombinator.com/topcompanies/ and have been profitable since 2022. We’re the leader in Long-Term Care staffing and are rapidly expanding into Home Health, Hospitals, and more, meaning we have more work to do than people to do it, and are growing our team to support millions more people and their communities.

THE ROLE

We're looking for an Applied Science Manager to build and lead Clipboard's Applied Science function, owning the roadmap and vision for science across the marketplace.

You'd be leading a small team of Applied Scientists and growing the function. The team owns the quantitative infrastructure underneath the marketplace: pricing algorithms, auction mechanisms, causal models, metric definitions, and experiment frameworks. Some of that work ships as product; some becomes the analytical substrate every team in the company depends on.

You'll set the bar for the function: defining our key metrics, how we measure them, and how we report on marketplace performance. Teams across product and engineering will build on the models, experiments, and insights your team produces.

This role sits at the intersection of engineering, product, finance, and operations. There will always be more valuable problems than the team can take on, so you'll decide what we work on, in what order, and what success looks like. That means balancing production work with analysis other teams depend on, knowing when a question requires careful causal identification versus a quick directional answer, and pushing back when the expected value isn't there. Priorities will shift, and you'll keep the team focused on the highest-impact work.

You'll also hire and develop the Applied Science team. This is a player-coach role: you'll mentor Applied Scientists across levels while staying close enough to the work to take on important IC problems yourself.

Our toolkit includes causal inference, machine learning, randomized experiments, discrete-time hazard models, auction/mechanism design, and time series analysis. You'll work directly with engineers to take models from prototype to production and communicate your reasoning clearly to PMs, operators, and leadership.

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS

- Bachelor’s degree in economics, statistics, engineering, mathematics, or another quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience.

- Experience building and deploying quantitative models in applied or research settings.

- Fluency querying data directly with SQL or an equivalent tool.

- Experience designing and analyzing controlled experiments.

- 1-3 years of experience managing or leading a team.

WHO THRIVES HERE

- PhD/Masters in economics, operations research, statistics, engineering, or a related field, or equivalent quantitative depth from research or trading.

- Track record of taking prediction models from idea to production.

- Strong grounding in experimental design and causal inference.

- Experience in quantitative finance, economic consulting, marketplaces, or another data-intensive environment where decisions have real business consequences.

Quick Note on Scammers:

Clipboard would never ask you for money or your bank details to participate in our hiring process. Report any scammers impersonating the Clipboard hiring team members here https://forms.gle/SyGaxHFbon7Hg9fW6.
